contributions.statement: When compiling a spec into per-module contracts, tag each requirement with its provenance (stated, inferred, delegated, unresolved) and route 'unresolved' items to a human before generation.
contributions.evidence: §3 design; Table 4 ablation (9 papers, single generation) favours reconciliation only on the reference-based score; all scores are an unvalidated o3-mini-high judge at ceiling, nothing executed (audit downgrades headline to weak).

contributions.statement: Per-file contracts generated from a spec do not by themselves prevent interface drift: API/schema mismatches rose from 2.3% to 4.0% under the contract-compiled pipeline.
contributions.evidence: §4.3 Table 3 human-categorised evaluator critiques; LLM-assigned severities.

reason: The provenance-tagged spec idea is relevant to SDD, but the only evidence is a ceiling-compressed LLM judge with no execution, and the paper's own ablation is mixed.
